questions: Are pieces allowed to move simultaneously in a single operation, or must each operation move exactly one piece?
If the graph contains cycles, is the minimum number of operations defined as the minimum over all possible sequences, including those where pieces might pass each other on an edge (if allowed)?
Is the piece movement constrained such that pieces cannot swap positions directly across an edge in one operation (since that would temporarily occupy the same vertex)?
Should the minimum operations count only moves of pieces, or does it include any other actions like waiting or no-ops?
If a piece moves to a vertex and the other piece later moves through that same vertex, is that allowed as long as they are never on the same vertex at the same time?
Are multiple moves of the same piece consecutively allowed, or must moves alternate between pieces?
Is the graph unweighted, meaning each edge move costs one operation regardless of edge properties?
If the minimum path requires pieces to temporarily be on vertices that are not on the shortest individual paths, is that considered in the minimization?
